new.headline: A clean first week back with the shin quiet and effort honest. Next week we hold to three days and nudge each run interval from roughly a minute and a half up to two minutes.

flags.title: Shin response
flags.detail: watch for any ache during the run or next morning stiffness, and stop the session if it appears.

flags.title: Session structure

flags.detail: total session time goes from 45 min to about 50 min, inside the small-step rule.

flags.title: Three-day rhythm

new.analysis:
Three sessions, three pain-free reports, and a steady heart rate around 121 to 123. That is the best possible first week back, so we add a little without changing the shape of the week.

The guiding rule for you right now is small steps: total running time up by about ten percent, longest continuous run up by no more than two to three minutes. You are bumping each run interval by roughly thirty seconds and adding one round on Saturday, which fits inside both limits.

The goal of running thirty minutes without walking by mid-October is still realistic if the shin keeps behaving. We will get there by lengthening the run portion a minute or so at a time and shrinking the walk, not by adding days or pushing pace.

One thing to carry into every session: if the shin aches at 3 out of 10 or above during the run, stop and walk home. If it is sore the next morning, we repeat the previous week instead of adding; that is how we protect the progress you just made.

settingsProposalBullets: Target: run 30 min continuously by mid-October, progressing walk-run intervals weekly if pain stays at 0 of 10.
Rule of thumb to log: stop the run if shin pain reaches 3 of 10, and repeat the prior week if it is sore the next morning.

safetyCallouts.title: Keep your physio in the loop.
safetyCallouts.body: Message them if the shin aches during a run, feels sore the next morning, or you notice any pinpoint tenderness on the bone, and pause running until they weigh in.
